exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal breech, primary cesarean, secondary cesarean)
cohort: Singleton pregnancies in breech presentation > 36.0 weeks of gestation between January 2018 and December 2019
finding: There was no significant difference in neonatal admission rates between vaginal breech delivery, primary cesarean section, and secondary cesarean section, but vaginal breech delivery was associated with a shorter NICU stay.
mod_finding: Vaginal breech delivery did not result in higher neonatal admission rates compared to cesarean sections, and NICU stays were shorter for infants delivered vaginally.
